pages.text: The mosque was roofed on trunks of palm trees, and when the Prophet ﷺ gave a sermon, he would stand by one of those trunks.
A woman of the Ansar, or a man, said: “O Messenger of Allah, shall we not make a minbar for you?” He said: “If you wish.” (Sahih al-Bukhari 3584)
So they made a minbar for him, and when Friday came, the Prophet ﷺ moved to the minbar.

The trunk cried out like a little child, and Jabir ibn Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: “We heard from that trunk a sound like the sound of the ishar” (Sahih al-Bukhari 3585) — the ishar are she-camels carrying young.

The Prophet ﷺ came down and held it close to him, and it began to moan like a little child being hushed; he ﷺ put his hand on it, and it became calm. And he said: “It was crying for the remembrance it used to hear near it.” (Sahih al-Bukhari 3584)
In this story, the trunk cried for the remembrance it used to hear, and the Prophet ﷺ came down to it, held it close, and put his hand on it until it became calm.
